title: Snakebite envenoming (India)
subject: toxicology
setting: Primary health centre, emergency department, ICU
summary: Immobilise and transport without tourniquets or incisions. Give polyvalent ASV IV, without a test dose, for systemic envenoming (incoagulable 20WBCT, bleeding, neuroparalysis, rapidly progressive swelling), same dose in children and pregnancy; add atropine-neostigmine and ventilation for neuroparalysis and be ready to treat ASV anaphylaxis.

sections.title: First aid and arrival
items: Reassure (about 70% of bites are non-venomous). Splint and immobilise the whole bitten limb like a fracture, keep the patient still, nil by mouth, and transport quickly (102/108 ambulance). The victim must not walk, run or drive.
Remove rings, bangles, watches, footwear and tight clothing from the bitten limb before swelling starts. Leave blisters alone.
Do not: tie tourniquets, cut or suck the wound, wash or rub it, apply herbs, black stone, ice or cautery, inject ASV locally, or try to catch or kill the snake.
If a tourniquet is already on, remove it slowly only after IV access, ASV and resuscitation are ready, as release can cause sudden deterioration.
On arrival: rapid primary survey for airway compromise, respiratory failure, shock or cardiac arrest. Admit every snakebite for at least 24 hours (NAPSE 2024).

sections.title: Recognise the syndrome
items: Neuroparalytic (cobra, krait): ptosis, diplopia, dysphagia, dysarthria, neck and limb weakness, respiratory paralysis.
Krait: often a painless night-time bite in a sleeping person with minimal local signs; may present with abdominal pain and then ptosis.
Vasculotoxic (Russell's viper, saw-scaled viper): painful swelling, blistering, spontaneous bleeding (gums, bite site, haematuria), incoagulable 20WBCT, shock and AKI (AKI not with saw-scaled viper).
Cobra: painful progressive swelling and local necrosis with neurotoxicity. Russell's viper in some regions (for example Tamil Nadu) can also cause paralysis.
Severe envenoming clues: rapidly spreading swelling, early tender regional lymph nodes, early spontaneous bleeding, dark urine, ptosis or breathing difficulty.

sections.title: 20WBCT and investigations
items: 20WBCT: put 2 mL of fresh venous blood in a new, clean, dry glass tube, leave undisturbed for 20 minutes at room temperature, then tilt. Still liquid means incoagulable blood (venom-induced consumption coagulopathy).

Baseline 20WBCT clotted and no envenoming: re-examine at 2, 6, 12 and 24 hours and repeat 20WBCT at 6, 12 and 24 hours after the bite (NAPSE 2024). Do not wait for 20WBCT if there is spontaneous systemic bleeding.
After ASV for coagulopathy, repeat 20WBCT 6 hours after each dose until blood clots.
Also: CBC and platelets, PT/INR, aPTT, creatinine, electrolytes, urine for blood or myoglobin, CK and ECG; single-breath count or peak flow in neuroparalysis. Group and cross-match the first sample.

sections.title: Antisnake venom (ASV)
items: Indications: systemic envenoming (incoagulable 20WBCT, spontaneous bleeding, neuroparalysis, shock, AKI, dark urine) or rapidly progressive local swelling. Purely local swelling, or swelling several hours old, is not an indication.

Give IV only, never IM or at the bite site. No test dose: skin and conjunctival tests do not predict reactions. Reconstitute each vial in 10 mL of water or saline and infuse diluted in normal saline (5 to 10 mL/kg) over 30 to 60 minutes.
Neuroparalytic: 10 vials IV over 30 minutes; a second 10 vials after 1 hour if no improvement. Maximum 20 vials; repeat if neurotoxic signs relapse.
Vasculotoxic, high-dose regimen (NAPSE 2024): 10 vials over 30 to 90 minutes, then 6 vials every 6 hours until 20WBCT clots and/or swelling subsides.

Vasculotoxic, low-dose infusion (MoHFW 2016, as effective and saves ASV): 10 vials (Russell's viper) or 6 vials (saw-scaled viper) over 30 minutes, then 2 vials every 6 hours in 100 mL saline until clotting normalises or for 3 days, whichever is earlier.
If 30 vials have been given, reconsider further ASV, especially without systemic bleeding. Persistent coagulopathy with bleeding: FFP 10 to 15 mL/kg, cryoprecipitate, or fresh whole blood.
Children and pregnant women receive the same ASV dose as adults. Late arrivals still get ASV if coagulopathy is present.
Indian polyvalent ASV does not neutralise hump-nosed pit viper or sea snake venom; do not give it for confirmed bites by these snakes.

sections.title: Neuroparalysis and ASV reactions
items: Bulbar or respiratory paralysis: intubate (or laryngeal mask) and ventilate; manual bag ventilation works if no ventilator is available. Deep coma may still recover fully, so do not diagnose brain death.

Atropine-neostigmine (AN): atropine 0.6 mg IV then neostigmine 1.5 mg IV; then neostigmine 0.5 mg with atropine every 30 minutes for 5 doses, then tapering doses at 1, 2, 6 and 12 hours. Children: atropine 0.05 mg/kg, neostigmine 0.04 mg/kg then 0.01 mg/kg.

AN response is positive if ptosis improves by 50% or more within 1 hour (suggests cobra). Stop if no response after 3 doses, or if fasciculations or bradycardia occur. Do not use in confirmed krait bite. Give one AN dose before transfer.

Early ASV reaction (itch, urticaria, fever, vomiting, bronchospasm, hypotension): stop ASV, adrenaline 0.5 mg IM of 1:1000 (children 0.01 mg/kg), chlorphenamine 10 mg IV (children 0.2 mg/kg), oxygen and fresh IV saline. Once settled, restart ASV slowly.

MoHFW 2016 advises prophylactic adrenaline 0.25 mg SC (children 0.005 mg/kg) before ASV except with hypertension or heart disease; keep adrenaline drawn up. Observe every 5 minutes for 30 minutes, then every 15 minutes for 2 hours.
Serum sickness (1 to 12 days later): chlorphenamine 2 mg every 6 hours for 5 days; if no response in 24 to 48 hours, prednisolone 5 mg every 6 hours for 5 days.

sections.title: Supportive care
items: Strict bed rest, no IM injections, intake-output chart and urine colour; keep urine output about 1 mL/kg/h.
Dialysis for hyperkalaemia, fluid overload with pulmonary oedema, severe acidosis, uraemic complications or rapidly rising creatinine; refer early if not available.
Do not use heparin or antifibrinolytics for snakebite coagulopathy.
Fasciotomy only for proven compartment syndrome and after coagulopathy is corrected; swelling and blistering alone are not indications. Give tetanus prophylaxis.

sections.title: Refer
items: Refer after starting ASV where possible if ASV, ventilation or dialysis are unavailable, or for bleeding, shock, AKI or respiratory weakness.
Send with a doctor or trained staff where possible, with airway equipment and a dose of AN given for neuroparalysis.
Unusual presentations or increasing complexity: consult a poisons information centre early (NAPSE 2024).

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Waiting for a 20WBCT result when there is spontaneous systemic bleeding, or withholding ASV for fear of reactions.
Giving ASV to every bite or for purely local swelling, or giving an incomplete dose.
Using a reused or wet tube for 20WBCT (false results).
Missing krait envenoming: painless bite, early morning abdominal pain, then ptosis.

drugs.name: Polyvalent antisnake venom (ASV)
drugs.dose: Neuroparalytic: 10 vials IV over 30 minutes, repeat 10 vials after 1 hour if no improvement (max 20). Vasculotoxic: 10 vials, then 6 vials every 6 hours (high dose) or 2 vials every 6 hours (low dose) until 20WBCT clots
drugs.notes: IV only, no test dose; same dose in children and pregnancy.

drugs.name: Neostigmine
drugs.dose: 1.5 mg IV, then 0.5 mg every 30 minutes for 5 doses, then taper at 1, 2, 6 and 12 hours (children 0.04 mg/kg, then 0.01 mg/kg)
drugs.notes: Always with atropine; stop if no response after 3 doses.

drugs.name: Atropine
drugs.dose: 0.6 mg IV with each neostigmine dose (children 0.05 mg/kg)

drugs.name: Adrenaline (epinephrine) 1:1000
drugs.dose: 0.5 mg IM for ASV anaphylaxis (children 0.01 mg/kg); prophylaxis 0.25 mg SC (children 0.005 mg/kg)
drugs.notes: Prophylaxis per MoHFW 2016; avoid prophylaxis in hypertension or heart disease.

drugs.name: Chlorphenamine
drugs.dose: 10 mg IV (children 0.2 mg/kg) for early reaction; 2 mg every 6 hours for 5 days for serum sickness

drugs.name: Fresh frozen plasma
drugs.dose: 10 to 15 mL/kg IV over 30 to 60 minutes
drugs.notes: Persistent bleeding with coagulopathy despite adequate ASV.
